1: Figure 1. Staged audit separates technical scoreability, phenotype-balanced representation and incremental phenotype information. a, Historical attrition from 137 strict to 132 not-known-incompatible and 42 structure-ready genes; the partner-qualified intermediate subset contained 128 genes. MutPred-PPI scored 10,917/11,150 submitted rows (97.91%), while only three genes were phenotype-balanced. b, Common-denominator C4 ≥70% and balanced counts for the disruption and sequence arms. c, Fifteen shared balanced genes yield ten phenotype-ready genes and 547 independent residues. Median ΔR² is 0.0018; the existing 95% gene-bootstrap CI includes zero and the frozen global rule fails. Counts are deterministic; thresholds and all three scientific verdicts remain frozen. Arrows indicate audit order rather than biological causation.
2: Figure 2. Sequence models extend representation availability under a shared denominator. Solid bars show genes with C4 ≥70%; hatched bars show phenotype-balanced genes. Methods retain fixed colors and appear in structural and sequence groups. All counts use the same 132-gene U2 denominator and are deterministic, without inferential intervals. Bars compare representation availability under the common denominator; score semantics differ across methods. These counts measure representation availability, not phenotype prediction.
3: Figure 3. Internal structural validity, partner-track variation and input-contract availability describe separate properties of sequence rescue. a, Existing macro AUROC and AUPRC estimates and 95% percentile CIs from 1,000 query-protein bootstrap resamples: SPPIDER-seq 80 proteins/63,687 residue–pair units and X-PAIR 67/51,928. Experimental contacts ≤5 Å define labels. b, Approximate frozen median within-gene pairwise partner-track Spearman summaries (0.926 and 0.745); higher similarity means less variation across partner tracks. No inferential interval was prespecified. c, Fixed 15,942-pair plan per model: 15,471 SPPIDER-seq and 13,094 X-PAIR scored pairs; X-PAIR has 2,377 MODEL_LENGTH_UNSUPPORTED pairs. Each model has 471 other unavailable pairs. Pair counts are deterministic; availability differs. Structural-validity metrics are internal and training overlap is unknown; they should not be interpreted as held-out model comparison.
4: Figure 4. The phenotype-ready primary cohort uses a narrower denominator than the broader residue registry. a, Fifteen shared balanced genes contain 1,034 unique pathogenic residues: 680 single-disease, 39 cross-disease and 315 multilabel/ambiguous. Only the eligible single-disease branch proceeds through the prospective ≥10-unique-residues-per-group gate to ten genes/547 primary residues, with median 17 common partners. b, All primary single-disease cohort group sizes; Group 1/2 follow frozen lexicographic MONDO order and do not denote common diseases across genes. c, All ten genes’ cross-disease-linked percentages use the broader annotated registry, including excluded discordant and multilabel records, rather than the safe single-disease primary cohort denominator in b. Counts and registry rates are deterministic without inferential intervals. The footer states the logical WT residue-context ceiling: substitutions at one position share a residue × partner vector. This limitation was not tested as the cause of the global result.
5: Figure 5. The preregistered partner-identity test did not meet the frozen global support rule. a, All ten genes’ X-PAIR ΔR² (labeled − sorted), in alphabetical frozen order with a zero reference. b, Paired labeled and sorted R² on identical residue rows, connected within each gene. Neither panel adds a per-gene CI. c, Equal-weight median ΔR²=0.00179553 with existing 95% CI [−0.00410526, 0.00495717] from 10,000 gene bootstrap resamples, seed 20261005. Condition A failed because the CI includes zero; Condition B passed because 8/10 effects were positive (threshold ≥70%); the A AND B global rule failed. The exact one-sided sign-test P=0.0546875 is descriptive here. d, All ten matched X-PAIR and SPPIDER-seq ΔR² values, with zero references and neutral RS1/COL3A1 labels. Frozen descriptive Spearman concordance is −0.745455; 4/10 genes are positive in both models. No cross-model interval is added and this comparison is not external validation.
S1: Supplementary Figure S1. Paired permutation-null example. Unchanged alphabetical-first COL3A1 display from the completed test. Histogram includes all 10,000 unique group-size-preserving alternative assignments, excluding observed labels. A solid blue line marks observed ΔR² and dashed gray zero. One-sided plus-one P counts null effects at least as large as observed. No gene was selected for significance. Source: saved COL3A1 paired permutation arrays.
S2: Supplementary Figure S2. Restricted permutation sensitivity. All ten genes’ unrestricted and restricted paired-contrast P values. Segments connect the same frozen gene. The dashed line is nominal P=0.05, not a new FDR gate. GUCY2D and LHCGR use all 1,763 and 3,149 alternatives; other genes use 10,000. Restricted strata were fixed before association. Status is concordant 10/10 and no primary decision changes. No inferential interval is attached to permutation P. Source: restricted result table.
S3: Supplementary Figure S3. Sequence length audit. a, X-PAIR length-supported partner counts against query length. b, SPPIDER scored partner counts with windowed full-sequence inference. Every gene with a known query length is shown; genes without canonical sequence length are unavailable, not zero-length proteins. The dashed 2,000-aa boundary marks X-PAIR’s upper contract limit, which also applies to partners. Counts are descriptive with no uncertainty. Sources: length constraint and long-sequence audits.
S4: Supplementary Figure S4. Per-gene common-denominator coverage. All 132 genes in alphabetical order, split into four panels for legibility. Columns show MutPred-PPI, structural binary, structural distance, SPPIDER and X-PAIR C4 fractions. C4 is the proportion of frozen common-primary variants with ≥3 valid credible partners. The stepped neutral color scale is fixed 0–1; white denotes unavailable values, not zero coverage. Every gene and all five methods are retained. Values are frozen coverage fractions without inferential intervals. Source: gene-level coverage table.
S5: Supplementary Figure S5. Deterministic partner replacement controls. a, True versus replacement-partner track Spearman for all 60 controls per sequence model. b, Existing mean absolute track differences for the same controls. SPPIDER-seq uses ochre circles and X-PAIR blue squares. Controls use 20 deterministic eligible genes and three partners each. The numerical index is plotting order and is not a new biological ranking. Replacement selection was phenotype-blind. No association test or uncertainty interval is added. Source: frozen shuffled-partner control table.
S6: Supplementary Figure S6. Computational resource accounting. Recorded CPU hours, peak RAM and embedding cache size for the two sequence arms. Decimal GB uses 10⁹ bytes. Values retain original measurement scopes: SPPIDER includes encoder/cache IO; X-PAIR batch-wall and measured-forward timings are separately recorded in Table S9. Busy GPU hours/peak VRAM are unavailable when not profiled. Points are single recorded accounting values without inferential intervals, and do not establish an equal-hardware speed ranking. Source: computational resource table.
S7: Supplementary Figure S7. Different complete-case gene sets prevent global ranking. Dots show existing equal-weight median paired X-PAIR-minus-baseline R² contrasts on each baseline’s row-matched evaluable set. POSITION n=10, GENERIC_INTERFACE n=5, GENERIC3D n=4 and DOMAIN_PROXY n=2 are explicitly labeled. The zero reference separates positive and negative contrasts. These are frozen descriptive medians without prespecified confidence intervals; no ranges or additional inference are introduced. Different complete-case gene sets prevent global ranking.
